title: Cost Curation Inspector: previewable batching & cache suggestions with reversible apply traces
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a Console 'Cost Curation Inspector' view that surfaces automated batching and KV-prefix caching recommendations, shows token-cost/latency delta previews, and provides a reversible 'safe apply' that records an immutable trace for audit and rollback.

Background: Customers running production inference often underutilize batching and prefix caching. The Optimize product already generates recommendations; this ticket is to design and deliver an inspector UI that makes those suggestions actionable, previewable (diffs against current config and estimated unit economics), and auditable with play-by-play traces for every apply.

Scope: UX flows for recommendation cards, side-by-side diff preview, confidence scoring for recommendation impact, safety checklist, apply modal with dry-run and canary scheduling, and an apply history UI that exposes who applied what, related PRs/rollouts, and one-click rollback to last-safe state.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation cards render for a target workload and include: recommendation summary, estimated tokens saved, estimated latency impact, confidence band, and 'why' rationale
Diff preview shows exact config delta (batch_size, max_latency_ms, cache_prefix_rules) with per-field simulated throughput/cost delta and percentile latency impact
Safe apply modal supports Dry Run, Canary (percentage rollout over time), and Immediate apply, with a mandatory safety checklist before enabling Immediate

Apply action creates an immutable audit entry visible in Apply History with timestamp, user, linked PR (if any), changed fields, simulated vs observed post-apply metrics, and 'rollback' button that reverts to previous config
System records telemetry events for recommendation shown, recommendation applied, dry-run executed, canary progression, and rollback executed
Design review approved by Platform UX and PM; ENG sign-off on APIs for dry-run and apply trace endpoints
notes: 2026-02-15: Initial problem discovery — Optimize recommendations have low adoption; customers cite lack of trust and fear of regressions
2026-02-18: Workshop with infra and serving teams to enumerate safe apply constraints (e.g., can't exceed node memory thresholds, enforce per-tenant RBAC)
2026-02-23: Prototype Figma v1 created; focuses on card-first browse flow and side-by-side diff; link in 'links' below
2026-03-01: Eng spike (ENG-4821) completed: implemented dry-run API that simulates batch and cache changes against recent traffic trace
2026-03-03: PM/Design sync — agreed to support canary ramp with automatic health checks and rollback-on-regression thresholds
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-02-16): 'We need to quantify customer pain — add a dashboard metric to measure recommendation click-to-apply conversion.'
Marco Nguyen (2026-02-19): 'Engineering spike assigned to ENG-4821 and ENG-4970 to validate dry-run fidelity. Early results show simulation error <3% for token-cost estimates.'
Leah Kim (Design, 2026-02-23): 'Figma prototype updated — moved confidence badge to top-right and added inline why-rationale.'
Ravi Shah (Infra, 2026-02-28): 'Constraint list: cache rules must respect tenant KV quota; batching increase can be blocked if measured memory pressure > 80%.'
UX Review (2026-03-02): 'Approve flow if audit entry includes pre/post metrics and rollback is one-click with automatic canary rollback option.'
implementation_notes: Use dry-run API from ENG-4821 to compute simulated post-apply metrics; integrate with Console preview UI
Backend: store audit entries in immutable apply_traces table with schema: trace_id, user, timestamp, delta_blob, pre_metrics, post_metrics_simulated, rollout_plan
Frontend: new Inspector route under /optimize/curation with lazy-loaded components; recommendation cards as cards list; diff preview in split panel
Telemetry: emit events optimize.recommendation.view, optimize.recommendation.apply.start, optimize.recommendation.apply.complete, optimize.recommendation.rollback
RBAC: only users with 'optimize.apply' scope can perform Immediate or Canary applies; dry-run allowed for broader role
design_feedback: Top-level metric banner should include estimated monthly $ savings and confidence interval
Cards must expose the critical config fields inline to reduce click-to-action friction
Diff preview color-coding: green for cost-reduction, amber for latency-increase, red for breaking changes (e.g., incompatible cache rules)
Add contextual help tooltips driven by our knowledge base links
risk_mitigation: Canary default to 10% for 30 minutes with automatic rollback on latency P95 degradation > 10%
Dry-run available to all users to build trust before enabling apply
Require a mandatory safety checklist for Immediate apply (quota checks, mem pressure, dev owner signoff for tenant-level changes)
Audit entries are write-once and signed with user id and request nonce to support compliance investigations
qa_plan: QA will validate with synthetic workloads: baseline traffic trace replay and compare simulated vs observed cost deltas; test canary ramp with intentional latency regressions to verify rollback automation; test RBAC cases and audit visibility; acceptance tests will be automated in console-e2e suite and linked to PR.
rollout_plan: Beta rollout to 5 internal customers (opt-in) for two weeks; collect adoption and regression metrics; ramp to GA after sign-off and runtime-1.19 release window. Enable feature flag optimize.costCurationInspector (staged by org).
